chunks: Prayer is not missed by one who intends the prayer. The daytime prayer is not missed until the sun sets, nor the night prayer until dawn rises, nor the dawn prayer until the sun rises.
And what further clarifies what we have mentioned is what he narrated:
Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb, from Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Faḍḍāl, from ʿAlī ibn Yaʿqūb al-Hāshimī, from Marwān ibn Muslim, from ʿUbayd ibn Zurārah, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

key_terms.الصَّلَاةُ: the prescribed salat (prayer) discussed in terms of its valid time
key_terms.تَطْلُعَ الشَّمْسُ: the rising of the sun marking the end of dawn prayer time
key_terms.تَغِيبَ الشَّمْسُ: the setting of the sun marking the end of daytime prayer time
key_terms.صَلَاةُ اللَّيْلِ: the night prayer whose time remains until dawn
key_terms.صَلَاةُ النَّهَارِ: the daytime prayer whose time remains until sunset
key_terms.صَلَاةُ الْفَجْرِ: the dawn prayer whose time remains until sunrise
key_terms.يَطْلُعَ الْفَجْرُ: the rising of dawn marking the end of night prayer time

ai.seo_question: Until when is a prayer considered not yet missed according to the hadith of Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the time limits within which the prescribed prayers are still considered performable and not yet missed. It clarifies the temporal range for daytime prayer, night prayer, and dawn prayer, showing the legal significance of prayer times in Islamic jurisprudence.
